overview: Guston was a dispersed high-altitude mining camp in the Red Mountain district rather than a formally gridded town.
Scan identification should use the broad historic camp landscape around the Guston/Robinson workings and former Silverton Railroad corridor.

timeline.text: Timeline: ore discoveries around the Guston area date to 1881–1882; secondary syntheses place settlement growth from 1883 and rapid development in the later 1880s.

The Silverton Railroad reached the Guston area by 1889.

Postal records summarized by secondary mining-history sources place a Guston post office at 1892–1898; the camp peaked around the early 1890s and sharply declined after the 1893 silver crisis and mine shutdowns by the late 1890s.
